synonyms: Bothriochloa laguroides subsp. torreyana (Steud.) Allred & Gould

accepted_taxonomy.source: Kew Plants of the World Online
accepted_taxonomy.taxonomic_mapping_note: Many Texas references and older herbarium treatments use Bothriochloa laguroides subsp. torreyana. That Texas entity is mapped here to the current accepted species Bothriochloa torreyana.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common native Central Texas bluestem and an essential comparison with invasive King Ranch bluestem and little bluestem.

target_zone_range.evidence_note: Current Kew treatment accepts B. torreyana and includes Texas in its native range. Texas Hill Country vouchers published under the older B. laguroides concept document Burnet, Crockett, Gillespie, Hays, and Val Verde; those records correspond to the Texas silver-bluestem entity historically treated as subsp. torreyana.

look_here_first: Start at the top: the seed head is a compact, conspicuously silky silver-white cluster of many racemes. If that looks right, drop to the leaf sheath—the sheath margins are villous, while the blade itself is comparatively broad and mostly glabrous.
project_tracker_diagnostic: Perennial bunchgrass with a conspicuously silver-white, silky terminal inflorescence; slightly compressed sheaths are keeled near the collar and have villous margins; blades are commonly 3–8 mm wide.

morphology_keys.habit: Cespitose bunchgrass without rhizomes or stolons; culms roughly 35–120 cm in Texas Hill Country material.
morphology_keys.nodes: Glabrous or pubescent, but not the conspicuous long 'beard node' of cane bluestem.
morphology_keys.sheaths: Slightly laterally compressed, keeled near the collar; outer surface mostly glabrous but sheath margins distinctly villous.
morphology_keys.collar: Continuous and glabrous; margins entire to sparsely villous.
morphology_keys.ligule: Membranous, about 1–3 mm, obtuse to truncate, margin erose.
morphology_keys.leaf_blades: Linear, about 3–6(–8) mm wide; flat to weakly keeled; mostly glabrous.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Terminal contracted panicle/cluster with many racemes; dense silky hairs on spikelets and rachis produce the characteristic silver-white plume.
best_field_traits: many racemes clustered at stem tip

lookalikes.separator: KR bluestem is not usually conspicuously plumose; its raceme branches extend beyond the short panicle axis and it commonly has papilla-based hairs on the blade just above the collar plus a ring of short hairs at the nodes.
Cane bluestem has a very conspicuous beard of long hairs (about 1–3 mm) around the culm nodes. Silver bluestem is better recognized by the silky terminal plume plus villous sheath margins.
Little bluestem bears single racemes at the ends of many lateral branches; silver bluestem groups many racemes into a compact terminal cluster.

culm plus leaf and inflorescence relationship

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Prioritize the silver plume and spikelet/awn structure; include a field habit and a stem/leaf context image.

ecology.habitat: Grasslands, prairies, roadsides, rocky slopes, and woodland margins; NPSOT lists Edwards Plateau and Texas Blackland Prairie among its ecoregions.
ecology.season: Warm-season; blooms through much of the warm season and remains conspicuous into fall.
